summary.headline: Sumitomo Chemical India Q2 FY27 revenue fell 2% to INR907 crores and EBITDA margin dropped to 20.5% on drought-hit volumes and inventory cost timing.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR907 crores, down 2% YoY, with volumes down a high single-digit percentage as a weak monsoon cut consumption. Gross margin fell 240 bps to 40.7% and EBITDA margin fell 297 bps to 20.5% because higher-cost inventory bought in April-June flowed through cost of sales. H1 revenue was INR1,971 crores (down 1%) and net profit rose 5% to INR372 crores including a one-time INR26.9 crore insurance income in Q1. Management said inventory costs normalised by end-Q2 and guided to normal H2 margins, while flagging H2 as challenging due to El Nino and low reservoir levels.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be challenging, but management expects stable revenue and margins within historical ranges, with no significant adverse factors projected.
Management aims to grow H2 sales over last year where the market allows while protecting profitability; prices to be adjusted product by product.
Inventory days expected to normalise through H2 FY27 from 115 days at September 2026.
Dahej greenfield herbicide intermediate (INR150 crore capex) expected to commercialise in Q2 FY28-29 (around July-October 2028); payback under 5 years, margins in line with company levels.
Tarapur capex of INR20 crores (two INR10 crore projects) adds 3-4 products; first part completes this FY, second part by end FY28.
Maintenance and debottlenecking capex of INR50-70 crores per year; no forward guidance given on special projects.
capex_capacity: Dahej greenfield site: INR150 crores for a dedicated intermediate for one herbicide; commercial production targeted Q2 FY28-29.
Tarapur: two INR10 crore capex projects adding 3-4 domestic-focused products; one part due this FY, second part by end FY28.
INDIFLIN: manufacturing at Tarapur for Indian demand by end of this FY; no capex approved for global export capacity.
Additional Dahej projects under evaluation with parent company; none approved yet.
demand_pricing: Industry H1 FY27 was one of the weakest first halves in over a decade: June rain about 35% below normal, season deficit about 13%, drought declared in several states.
Kharif acreage about 1.5% below normal; rice down about 4%. Crop output for key crops estimated about 10% lower.
Selling prices held largely stable in Q2 after Mar-Jun 2026 price increases; industry price cuts from June onward.
Key brands (SumiMax, Meshi, Excalia Max, Portion, ProGibb, Nature Dip, TriBasic Copper) grew about 22% in value in H1.
Exports to parent company Japan were hit by parent-company inventory liquidation; Japan exports almost halved in H1. Third-party exports grew, led by Africa, Europe and Brazil.
Volume impact on exports about 10% in the current year.
Paraquat ban by the Government of India may open space for glyphosate; management sees possible upside but no quantification.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the semiconductor chemicals opportunity and India entity's role?
qa_highlights.answer: Parent Sumitomo Chemical Japan signed an MOU with an Indian semiconductor player; SCIL is part of strategic discussions but no concrete structure or role has been defined. A new announcement is expected in the next few months once more certain.

qa_highlights.question: Sales returns and need for higher provisions in H2 given elevated inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no formal sales return policy, returns are very low, and the team managed inventory build so almost all stock is liquidated. No H2 impact expected from returns.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 revenue run rate dip well below historical levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focusing on regions with good rains (UP, Chhattisgarh, parts of AP, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu). Grape, cumin and wheat outlook is reasonable, and it is preparing for a non-normal season.

qa_highlights.question: Is any H2 margin pressure expected?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO-level guidance: H2 margins expected in the normal historical range. Raw material cost delta seen as nothing negative currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Dahej herbicide plant timeline Q2 FY28 and what future capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercialisation is expected in Q2 FY28-29 (around July-October 2028), same timeline as announced in January 2026. Future capex is not guided beyond INR50-70 crores maintenance per year.

qa_highlights.question: Why not diversify, and why not return the cash of about INR2,500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees growth in agro, environmental health and animal nutrition, and believes Indian deployment is attractive. It will take return-of-cash to the Board if cash stays unused.

risks_watch: Strong El Nino expected to peak around December and continue to February 2027, overlapping the Rabi season; reservoir levels about 71% of capacity, at least 25% below last year.
Parent-company inventory liquidation in Japan and other markets may keep export volumes soft through H2 FY27.
Inventory days at 115 (vs 95 a year ago) and working capital at 76 days; management targets normalisation in H2.
Semiconductor opportunity remains unannounced at the Indian entity level; role of SCIL undefined.
Management declined to give export growth guidance or forward-looking estimates for capex and new projects.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on the near term and confident on direction: management repeatedly called H2 challenging yet guided to stable margins. It was evasive on the semiconductor opportunity, on export growth and on cash deployment, offering no timelines or numbers.
key_quotes: Our Q2 margins were affected by the timing of inventory cost.
This is broadly in line with our historical levels and in line with our objectives, which we have discussed in the past, to maintain our EBITDA margins equal to or more than 20% level
As our policy we do not give any forward -looking estimates or a forecast.

We remain cautious on the near term, but confident in our direction; a differentiated portfolio, deep farmer and channel relationships, a strong pipeline from our parent company and a team now focused on taking the company from Good to Great.
